---
title: Standalone API Worker
description: Manifest, policy, client generation, and retained-origin boundaries for apps/api.
---

`apps/api` is the standalone Cloudflare Worker foundation for `/api/*`. Its
entrypoint is `fetch(Request, env, ctx)`. It pins `nodejs_compat` and the
compatibility date to `2026-06-20`. The committed configuration has no zone
routes, custom domains, preview URLs, or workers.dev publication. Deployment and
traffic changes belong to the release owner.

## Registry and middleware

Export domain operations from `src/domains/` through `src/routes.ts`. Use
`defineRoute` with a unique operationId, HTTP method, `/api/...` pattern, explicit
policy, Zod input/output schemas, limits, aliases, and error encoding. Route
parameters use OpenAPI braces, such as `/api/v1/workspaces/{wsId}/documents`.
Services receive the resolved principal, request ID and AbortSignal through
`RequestContext`. Keep database access in existing domain services and inject it
through adapters. Do not add framework imports to portable services.

The pipeline canonicalizes and matches the request, checks CORS and body/deadline
budgets, runs the shared guard, resolves the principal once, verifies authorization
evidence, parses input, runs the handler, validates output, and emits allowlisted
native console metrics. Logs omit URLs, resource IDs, identities, credentials,
request/response bodies, and exception messages. Timeouts never retry a handler.
A write that outlives a timeout needs reconciliation with its original operation
or idempotency key.

`SecurityAdapter.guard` must preserve the active Web proxy's malformed Supabase
cookie, suspicious anonymous traffic, abuse/cost, bans, rate and payload controls.
Its principal resolver must preserve cookie/Bearer, audience, capability and
service distinctions. Its authorizer must verify membership and permissions,
including guest restrictions and root-admin permissions. The pipeline checks
workspace evidence and object ownership against path parameters; an API key or
external app must also match its bound workspace and scope.

**Protected routes return 503 until a verified concrete security adapter is
installed.** The foundation does not claim Web proxy parity from interfaces or
fixtures. Only the three named public metadata examples have a closed exemption.
The `ratePolicy` descriptor is an adapter contract; production rate/cost parity
still requires the concrete guard. No ordinary route may use this exemption.

The initial `defineRoute` adapter supports JSON responses and absent/JSON request
bodies. Streaming, signed raw webhooks, binary responses and redirects require
explicit additional transport contracts before registration. Do not label those
payloads `z.unknown()` or consume signed bytes in JSON middleware.

## Dispatch and retained origin

`API_WORKER_OPERATIONS` is a comma-separated allowlist of accepted operationIds.
Its default is empty: registering or merging code does not activate an operation.
Only an explicitly enabled operation wins over the retained inventory for its
method/path. Removing its ID restores retained dispatch; an unenabled new path
without a retained owner fails closed. Ops owns this per-operation flip and rollback.
`generated/retained-routes.json` records every live Web route source and its
SHA-256. These are retained Next operations, not completed Worker ports.
Unregistered paths return 404. Retained requests require `RETAINED_API_ORIGIN`:
an HTTPS deployment hostname outside `*.tuturuuu.com`, without credentials,
query, fragment or path. Pin it to an origin that bypasses the public Worker.

Forwarding preserves the raw body, method, auth and cookie headers. It strips
hop-by-hop and untrusted internal/forwarding headers, tags one hop, follows no
redirects, and performs no retries. A returned hop marker fails closed. The
retained Next application continues owning its proxy and route authorization.
Before any traffic flip, ops and the auth owner must verify trusted client IP,
canonical host/CSRF, repeated Set-Cookie, redirects, signatures and origin
availability against that exact retained deployment. The foundation alone does
not establish those deployment-specific contracts.

The dispatch table lives in `apps/api`; no extra router Worker is needed for
workspace IDs in the middle of a path. Keep sharp, bcrypt, Firebase Admin and
persistent ChatGPT filesystem graphs on their existing Node/self-hosted owner.
Do not import their graphs into the Worker to claim registry coverage.

## Mobile version contract

The consolidated mobile endpoint is
`GET /api/v1/mobile/version?platform=ios|android&build=<integer>`.
`MOBILE_VERSION_POLICY` is JSON with both platform entries:

```json
{
  "ios": {
    "minimumSupportedBuild": 42,
    "latestBuild": 50,
    "storeUrl": "https://apps.apple.com/app/example"
  },
  "android": {
    "minimumSupportedBuild": 12,
    "latestBuild": 15,
    "storeUrl": "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=example"
  }
}
```

These are fixture values, not production thresholds. Missing/invalid policy
returns 503. A build below its platform floor receives `requiresUpdate: true`
and `status: update-required`. At the floor, the build is supported; below the
latest build it receives `update-recommended`. Responses are never cached.
The mobile lane owns the forced-update screen and switches to consolidated
contracts immediately under the program decision. External non-mobile aliases
retain their existing wire contracts. The old semantic-version endpoint remains
on the retained origin until its separate disposition is reviewed.

Regression coverage lives in `apps/api/src/pipeline.test.ts`, with real emitted
Worker acceptance in `scripts/worker-runtime.test.mjs`.

## Generation and verification

Run `bun run --cwd apps/api generate` after changing contracts or the Web route
inventory. Commit the OpenAPI 3.1 spec, manifest, retained inventory and generated
TypeScript/Dart clients together. `registry:check` fails stale artifacts and
unregistered authored operation IDs. The first client generator supports the
foundation JSON schema subset and fails on unsupported schemas; extend it with
contract tests before adding new transports or complex schemas. Shared app HTTP
consumers remain under `packages/internal-api`; mobile may inject its HTTP
transport into the generated Dart client.

`.github/workflows/api-worker.yaml` checks the exact PR head with frozen
installation, registry checks, unit/contract tests, type, lint, real Vite+ Worker
build and an emitted-runtime smoke using Wrangler's local workerd harness. There
is no deploy step. The build uses `vp build --configLoader runner` until the
shared preset loader fix is accepted.

Run heavy checks on Thanh through one `ttr resources run -- <job>` admission.
Never build on the M4. If M4 disk admission rejects `check:changed`, transfer the
owned commit using a git bundle, verify its SHA in an isolated Thanh checkout,
and run the unchanged gate there. Never bypass the disk gate. Independent
security review, staging contracts, rollback rehearsal and ops approval remain
required before a direct per-unit production flip.


## Retained-route safety and origin attribution

Every retained entry declares `sideEffects` and `shadow`. Unknown operations are
`shadow: "never"`; `/api/v1/exchange-rates` and `/api/cron/**` explicitly declare
writes and prohibit shadow/replay. The exchange-rate GET can seed data through a
cron POST. Any future shadow/replay consumer must call
`assertShadowReplayAllowed`, which requires both an explicit `shadow: "safe"`
and `sideEffects: "read-only"` marker plus GET/HEAD. Only the audited health and
build-info metadata reads initially have that marker.

Generation fails if a broad Worker pattern could capture a more specific retained
pattern that has no Worker registration, including aliases and intersecting
parameter patterns. Register the specific path before the generic path. A method
or requested preflight method owned only by the retained origin is forwarded;
new Worker-only paths still return 405 for unsupported methods.

The retained inventory covers `apps/web/src/app/api/**/route.ts` source files.
Rewrite-only and proxy-only destinations are not discovered by that scan. Check
Next rewrites and proxy ownership separately before selecting a production cohort;
the filesystem inventory is not a complete routing map.

Worker forwarding requires the existing `TRUSTED_PROXY_ORIGIN_SECRET` and a valid
Cloudflare ingress `cf-connecting-ip`. It replaces caller-supplied
`x-tuturuuu-origin-auth` with a versioned HMAC-SHA256 proof of the canonical client
IP and timestamp. The proof uses the existing origin secret, remains valid for
60 seconds, and permits at most five seconds of future clock skew. It carries no
raw key. Missing/weak keys or invalid ingress addresses stop forwarding with 503.

The retained Next origin must use `TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare-origin` and the same
secret. Its shared resolver verifies the proof before deriving rate-limit keys.
The raw-secret apex Transform Rule and direct-origin Vercel fallback continue to
work. The proof authenticates client-IP attribution; existing session, permission
and provider signature verification still run. Rotation changes the existing
secret on both ends through the origin-trust runbook. Do not activate an operation
before this contract and the exact retained deployment have passed acceptance.

The build-free `check:changed` gate may discover the emitted-runtime test in a
cold checkout. When `dist/worker/wrangler.json` is absent, discovery reports a
clear skip without loading Wrangler or creating a harness. Explicit
`bun run --cwd apps/api test:runtime` requires the artifact and fails if it is
missing; CI runs that strict command after the real Worker build. An existing
artifact always runs the runtime assertions, so a skip is never runtime proof.

Automatic Worker invocation logs are disabled because they can include URLs and
queries. Application request events retain their allowlisted metadata and request
IDs. This setting does not make a claim about other platforms' logs.
